title: add-kms-policy-heuristics-and-audit-latency-sanitizer
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: some tenant flows choose KMS providers deterministically based on service tags; in practice this leads to increased cross-region key usage when tenants have multi-zone services and noisy routing. This PR adds a compact heuristic layer (policy_heuristics) to make KMS provider selection resilient to transient routing noise and to prefer region-local keys when the tenancy policy allows. In addition, we introduce an audit latency sanitizer that buckets high-cardinality downstream latency values for KMS calls to reduce sensitive telemetry leakage while preserving SLO monitoring fidelity.

What this changes: adds a policy heuristics module that evaluates candidate KMS providers using: region affinity score, tenant-declared residency preference, capability score (supports signed-requests, encryption-context tags), and a recent-success sliding window. It implements a short-circuit quarantine for ephemeral requests that have no declared residency: the request is routed to a safe default KMS and the tenant is flagged for a follow-up consent/claim-resolution flow. The audit latency sanitizer changes the audit pipeline to replace raw KMS call durations >250ms with a bucketed label ("<250ms","250-500ms",">500ms") and optionally fuzzy-timestamping for >2s latencies when configured by the tenant.

Backward compatibility and rollout: heuristics are off by default and gated behind the feature flag kms.policy_heuristics.enabled; sanitizer is opt-in per-tenant via tenancy flags. Rollout plan: start with 5 Canary customers for 2 weeks, observe error rates and audit fidelity; then stage to 20% of traffic with gradual ramp. Migration notes: existing KMS routing tables remain untouched; heuristics produce a deterministic hash-stable decision to avoid churn across restarts.

Security considerations: heuristics run inside the control plane and do not leak tenant secrets. Sanitizer preserves the original latency in the secure audit store (encrypted) for compliance retrieval; only streaming metrics are bucketted. We added KMS call signing to ensure we can verify provider responses when fallback occurs.

Testing and validation: unit + deterministic property tests added for edge cases (provider flapping, missing residency claim, signed-request failures). Integration test against gcp-emu and local-kms test harness included. Load test shows 0.8% p90 latency increase at 95th percentile on the control plane decision path at 10k qps, within the SLA budget.

Docs and observability: added webapp/docs/security/kms-heuristics.md and console toggles for per-tenant sanitizer opt-in; new dashboard shows heuristic decisions, quarantine counts, and sanitizer bucketing ratios.

Why now: recent incidents (SUP-891) showed repeated cross-region KMS usage spikes from transient routing changes; this is a lightweight mitigation that reduces blast radius and improves audit privacy for high-volume tenants.
